details: Existing text embedding benchmarks (BEIR, MTEB) evaluate mainly traditional passage retrieval and do not test retrieval of fragmented, context-dependent, temporally distant memories needed by memory-augmented agent systems.

LMEB: a zero-shot retrieval benchmark for memory embeddings, comprising 22 English datasets and 193 tasks converted into a unified IR-style schema (queries/corpus/qrels plus optional bounded candidate pools), built on and compatible with the MTEB evaluation framework.
Organizing principle: a four-way memory taxonomy (episodic, dialogue, semantic, procedural) positioned along axes of abstraction level and temporal dependency.

Episodic: EPBench, KnowMeBench; Dialogue: LoCoMo, LongMemEval, REALTALK, TMD, MemBench, ConvoMem; Semantic: QASPER, NovelQA, PeerQA, Covid-QA, ESG-Reports, MLDR (en), LooGLE, SciFact; Procedural: Gorilla, ToolBench, ReMe, Proced_mem_bench, MemGovern, DeepPlanning.
Retrieval granularities span event-, turn-, round-, session-, sentence-, paragraph-, tool-, and trajectory/experience-level; mix of AI-generated and human-annotated queries/corpora.

Queries with relative time expressions get an explicit query-time anchor appended; timestamps and session/round metadata encoded in corpus title/text; candidates file restricts retrieval to e.g. a query's own conversation history.
Long documents (LooGLE, NovelQA) chunked with semchunk at chunk size 256.
Primary metric NDCG@10 (also capped Recall@k, MAP, MRR, Precision); Mean (Dataset) aggregation as in MTEB.
Two query settings: w/o instruction and w/ instruction (instruction prepended as 'Instruct: {task instruction}\nQuery: q').
Max input length 1024 tokens (512 for multilingual-e5-large-instruct and bge-large-en-v1.5); 4 NVIDIA H100 GPUs; supports Transformers, Sentence-Transformers, vLLM backends.

15 embedding models from ~300M to ~12B parameters: Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B/4B/8B, KaLM-Embedding-V1/V2.5/Gemma3-12B, bge-m3 (Dense), bge-multilingual-gemma2, bge-large-en-v1.5, NV-Embed-v2, e5-mistral-7b-instruct, multilingual-e5-large-instruct, EmbeddingGemma-300M, jina-v5-text-nano/small (retrieval-optimized).

Inter-dataset diversity via pairwise weighted Jaccard similarity over unigram distributions, plus force-directed 2D layout (NetworkX); procedural datasets excluded from the 2D plot as weakly connected outliers.
Pearson and Spearman correlation of LMEB (overall and per memory type) scores against MTEB (eng, v2) retrieval subset scores.

key_findings.finding: LMEB and MTEB retrieval measure essentially orthogonal capabilities.
key_findings.evidence: Across the 15 models, LMEB Mean (Dataset) NDCG@10 versus MTEB (eng, v2) retrieval subset yields Pearson -0.115 and Spearman -0.130.

key_findings.finding: Transfer from passage retrieval is worst for dialogue and episodic memory, and only partial for semantic and procedural memory.
key_findings.evidence: LMEB-Dialogue vs MTEB correlations are Pearson -0.496 / Spearman -0.364; LMEB-Semantic 0.103 / 0.061; LMEB-Procedural 0.291 / 0.429 (the highest, attributed to overlap with tool/code retrieval training).

key_findings.finding: Model scale does not reliably predict long-horizon memory retrieval performance.
key_findings.evidence: Under the w/o instruction setting, the large KaLM-Embedding-Gemma3 (12B) and bge-multilingual-gemma2 underperform much smaller EmbeddingGemma-300M and bge-m3 (Dense).

key_findings.finding: The benchmark is challenging but tractable, leaving substantial headroom.
key_findings.evidence: The best model, bge-multilingual-gemma2 with instructions, reaches only 61.41 Mean (Dataset) NDCG@10.

key_findings.finding: Sensitivity to task instructions is model-dependent rather than uniformly beneficial.
key_findings.evidence: Ten models (e.g. KaLM-Embedding-Gemma3, Qwen3-Embedding series, e5-mistral-7b-instruct) improve with instructions; NV-Embed-v2 and jina-v5-text-small are insensitive; bge-m3 (Dense), bge-large-en-v1.5, and EmbeddingGemma-300M do better without them.
